title: Week 16 · Overview — Mission power · Wind and water turbines
bodyHtml:
Academic week of Monday, April 26, 2027 · 5 days · ≈9 B/C meetings · Phase 4: Power it, prove it — Generation & the Capstone · electromagnetism · Core week

Energía para la misión · Turbinas de viento y agua

The week in one paragraph

Every mission needs power, and a generator is the motor run backwards. A DC motor with blades on it, a fan or a tap. How much comes out, compared with what went in?

Learning targets

I can…Puedo…TypeWhat counts as evidence
I can explain that spinning a magnet past a coil makes a current — the motor run backwards.Puedo explicar que girar un imán frente a una bobina produce una corriente — el motor al revés.Knowledgerecall or recognition — a selected response or a labelled diagram is enough
I can measure electrical power out with voltage and current.Puedo medir la potencia eléctrica de salida con voltaje y corriente.Skillwatched while it is done, or read off the numbers it produced
I can estimate mechanical power in and report the turbine's efficiency.Puedo estimar la potencia mecánica de entrada e informar la eficiencia de la turbina.Reasoningthe graded evidence of this course — a claim with the evidence behind it
I can predict which blade change raises efficiency and test it.Puedo predecir qué cambio en las aspas aumenta la eficiencia y probarlo.Reasoningthe graded evidence of this course — a claim with the evidence behind it

Scored 1–2–3 per target (Marzano) on the reasoning artifact, lowest-dimension rule across the four dimensions. Targets carry Spanish in the app (statement_es), so the paper rating strip and the screen match.

Language objective (posted, tracked, never graded)

WIDA domainLevel 1 (Entering) will…Level 3+ will…Student line (ES)
WritingComplete "V = ____, I = ____, P = ____."Write efficiency with the estimate of power in.Completo V, I y P.

Read aloud at the start of every block with the content objective. Recorded met / not yet on the walk-around, by name, and reported to the ELL team — never in the physics grade.

The asteroid thread

What the shop knowsHow this week connects
Phase 4 opens: the shop has an arm, an ear, an actuator and comms. None of it runs without power.Spinning a magnet past a coil makes a current. Power out over power in is the efficiency the mission's power engineer signs for.

The arc of the week

DayHands (first)Into the app
1
Mon 26 Apr		Motor as generator: spin by hand, read voltage; blades v1 on the fanVoltage vs. spin
2
Tue 27 Apr		Power out with Vernier voltage + current probes and a load resistorP = V·I table
3
Wed 28 Apr		Mechanical power in (fan speed / water flow estimate); efficiencyEfficiency
4
Thu 29 Apr		Predict ONE blade change; lock; testPredicted / actual
5
Fri 30 Apr		Reasoning artifact + rate yourselfThe artifact

Every meeting: hands → record → talk (pairs, either language) → write (the tiered frame). Each segment ends with something saved. For this section the app is the packet — there is no paper page to copy.

Reasoning artifact — the graded evidence

Power out vs. your estimate of power in, the efficiency, and your tested prediction about the one blade change.

Potencia de salida frente a tu estimación de potencia de entrada, la eficiencia y tu predicción probada sobre el único cambio de aspas.

Off-week question

Where does the electricity at your shop come from? Follow it back one step. What is spinning?

¿De dónde viene la electricidad de tu taller? Síguela un paso hacia atrás. ¿Qué está girando?

Issued on the last day, nothing due, nothing late. It opens the next on-week.

Materials and tools

Small DC motors, blade kits, fan, Vernier voltage + current probes

Order, borrow or build anything missing during the off-week before this one — the shop week is the only slack in the calendar. Put the week's six to eight words on the bilingual word wall with icons before day 1.

Vocabulary — the wall, the lesson, the glossary and the games all read this list

TierWordEspañolWhat it meansIn this week
1blade (noun)aspaOne arm of a turbine.Change one blade and test.
1fan (noun)ventiladorThe wind source.Point the fan at the turbine.
2estimate (verb)estimar ≈Find an approximate number.Estimate the power going in.
2output (noun)salidaWhat comes out.Electrical output is V times I.
3generator (noun)generador ≈A device that turns spinning into current.A generator is a motor run backwards.
3induction (noun)inducción ≈A changing magnetic field making a current.Induction is why spinning the magnet makes current.
3voltage (noun)voltaje ≈The electric push, in volts.Read the voltage while it spins.
3turbine (noun)turbina ≈Blades that catch wind or water to spin a shaft.The turbine drives the generator.

Beck tiers: 3 is the physics word, 2 is the academic verb the frames are built from, 1 is the everyday word the demonstration needs. ≈ marks a cognate — say it as one out loud. ≠ marks a false friend — name the trap before it bites. Never introduce a word without the object in hand.

Standards

HS-PS2-5, HS-PS3-3

Where this week lands — Phase 4 mastery task

This week's artifact is evidence toward pp.t4.mastery-defend-a-redesign, the Phase 4 mastery task. The full task is on the overview for the last week of this phase.

The rules that do not change

  1. Hands first, always. The block opens with the object doing the thing. The explanation arrives after there is a result to explain — never a mini-lecture the build is waiting behind.
  2. The prediction is locked before the test, and it is scored on the reasoning, never on being right.
  3. The reasoning artifact is the grade. Whether the bridge held is recorded on its own product target and is never folded into the reasoning score.
  4. Spanish evidence is full evidence. A labelled diagram, a frame from the word bank and a spoken explanation in Spanish earn a 3 on a physics target exactly as an English paragraph would. Say it out loud, in both languages, every week.
  5. Nothing is graded that a WIDA Level 1 student could not have reached. Walk the artifact as that student before you rate anyone.

Full spec: the SEI access layer and the year map in the Claude project. The four-segment block — hands · record · talk · write, about 25 minutes each — is the shape of every meeting.

No day-by-day plans written for this week yet. Say the word and they get the same treatment as Weeks 1 and 2: segment timings and materials, the Spanish for the day, the formative checks and the misconception to press.

title: Week 18 · Overview — Mission review II · Test and defend

Same conditions as the original. Test. Then stand up and defend it — in either language — to a review board that has your first-round artifact in front of them.

Learning targets

I can…Puedo…TypeWhat counts as evidence

I can defend the redesign to a panel using my reasoning artifacts from both rounds.Puedo defender el rediseño ante un panel usando mis artefactos de razonamiento de ambas rondas.Reasoningthe graded evidence of this course — a claim with the evidence behind it
I can say plainly whether the redesign worked, and what the numbers say caused the result.Puedo decir claramente si el rediseño funcionó, y qué dicen los números que causó el resultado.Reasoningthe graded evidence of this course — a claim with the evidence behind it

Scored 1–2–3 per target (Marzano) on the reasoning artifact, lowest-dimension rule across the four dimensions. Targets carry Spanish in the app (statement_es), so the paper rating strip and the screen match.

WIDA domainLevel 1 (Entering) will…Level 3+ will…Student line (ES)

title: Week 19 · Overview — Arrival · Portfolio and final self-assessment
bodyHtml:
Academic week of Monday, June 7, 2027 · 4 days · ≈7 B/C meetings · Phase 4: Power it, prove it — Generation & the Capstone · metacognition · Support week (no new core target)

Llegada · Portafolio y autoevaluación final

The week in one paragraph

2026-XJ arrives around graduation. Every artifact of the year, the timeline as the cover page. Re-rate. Find the one where your reasoning changed.

Learning targets

I can…Puedo…TypeWhat counts as evidence
I can assemble every reasoning artifact of the year and re-rate myself against the targets.Puedo reunir todos los artefactos de razonamiento del año y reevaluarme frente a las metas.Skillwatched while it is done, or read off the numbers it produced
I can point to the artifact where my reasoning got better, and say what changed.Puedo señalar el artefacto donde mi razonamiento mejoró, y decir qué cambió.Reasoningthe graded evidence of this course — a claim with the evidence behind it

Scored 1–2–3 per target (Marzano) on the reasoning artifact, lowest-dimension rule across the four dimensions. Targets carry Spanish in the app (statement_es), so the paper rating strip and the screen match.

Language objective (posted, tracked, never graded)

WIDA domainLevel 1 (Entering) will…Level 3+ will…Student line (ES)
